card_summary: Tapestry Orchestration Platform's momentum signals a shift towards microservices-based workflow automation, likely leveraging Kubernetes for scalability and API orchestration for seamless integration with MAM systems. This architecture enables more efficient management of object storage, such as S3, and reduces egress costs. In practice, this means engineering teams must carefully evaluate the trade-off between the benefits of automated workflow orchestration and the potential complexity of integrating multiple microservices, which can increase the total cost of ownership if not properly managed.

Orchestration Platforms Gain Traction: What Broadcasters Need to Know About Scalability and Cost

As the broadcast industry continues to shift towards more efficient and scalable workflows, the appointment of a new reseller for an orchestration platform is a significant development. This move indicates a growing demand for solutions that can streamline media workflows, reduce operational overhead, and improve content delivery. With the rise of cloud infrastructure and object storage, broadcasters are looking for ways to optimize their workflows and minimize egress costs. The ability to automate workflows and integrate with existing systems, such as MAM and API orchestration, is becoming increasingly important.

Domain Signal Extraction

  • Broadcast technologies: The development of orchestration platforms touches on several broadcast technologies, including microservices, Kubernetes, and cloud-based workflows. Adjacent technologies affected include content delivery networks (CDNs), streaming protocols such as HLS and DASH, and digital rights management (DRM) systems.
  • Architecture layer: This development lands in the workflow automation and orchestration layer, specifically in the areas of ingest, processing, and delivery. It also has implications for the integration of cloud-based services, such as object storage and egress cost management.
  • Cybersecurity surface: The cybersecurity surface of this development is relatively low, as it primarily involves the automation of workflows and integration with existing systems. However, the use of microservices and cloud-based infrastructure does introduce some security considerations, such as the need for secure API orchestration and access control.
  • Business signal: The underlying commercial pressure driving this development is the need for broadcasters to reduce costs, improve efficiency, and increase scalability. The industry is responding to the growing demand for online content and the need to deliver high-quality experiences to viewers across multiple platforms.

Technology Intelligence

The appointment of a new reseller for an orchestration platform is a significant development in the broadcast industry, as it indicates a growing demand for solutions that can streamline media workflows and improve content delivery. In the next 12-18 months, we can expect to see a greater emphasis on workflow automation, cloud-based infrastructure, and object storage. The use of microservices and Kubernetes will become more prevalent, as broadcasters look to optimize their workflows and reduce operational overhead. One of the key challenges will be managing egress costs, as the amount of data being transferred between cloud-based services continues to grow. The development of standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS will also play a crucial role in the integration of cloud-based services and the automation of workflows.

Why This Matters

  • Broadcasters: The impact of this development on broadcasters will be significant, as it will enable them to reduce operational overhead, improve content delivery, and increase scalability. Regional broadcasters, in particular, will benefit from the ability to automate workflows and integrate with existing systems, such as MAM and playout automation. The reduced operational overhead will also enable broadcasters to allocate more resources to content creation and acquisition.
  • Streaming platforms: The impact on streaming platforms will be felt in the areas of content delivery and latency. The use of orchestration platforms will enable streaming platforms to improve their content delivery networks (CDNs) and reduce latency, resulting in a better viewer experience. The development of standards such as HLS and DASH will also play a crucial role in the delivery of high-quality content to multiple platforms.
  • Cybersecurity risk: The cybersecurity risk associated with this development is relatively low, as it primarily involves the automation of workflows and integration with existing systems. However, the use of microservices and cloud-based infrastructure does introduce some security considerations, such as the need for secure API orchestration and access control.
  • Market impact: The market impact of this development will be significant, as it will enable broadcasters and streaming platforms to improve their content delivery and reduce operational overhead. Vendors such as Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure will benefit from the growing demand for cloud-based infrastructure and object storage. The development of standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS will also drive the adoption of cloud-based services and workflow automation.

Key Technologies in Context

  • Object Storage (S3): Object storage will play a crucial role in the development of orchestration platforms, as it will enable broadcasters to store and manage large amounts of data in a scalable and efficient manner.
  • Microservices: Microservices will be used to build and deploy orchestration platforms, enabling broadcasters to automate workflows and integrate with existing systems in a flexible and scalable way.
  • Kubernetes: Kubernetes will be used to manage and orchestrate microservices, enabling broadcasters to deploy and manage containerized applications in a scalable and efficient manner.

Hidden Implications

  • The integration of orchestration platforms with existing systems, such as MAM and playout automation, will require significant investment in API development and integration. This will introduce new complexities and challenges, such as managing multiple APIs and ensuring seamless integration.
  • The development of standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS will drive the adoption of cloud-based services and workflow automation, but it will also introduce new complexities and challenges, such as managing multiple protocols and ensuring interoperability.

Editorial Perspective
